html:
SMTO-CFG-0078 — A Skill set to Always isn't allowed for this request

GUID: 0b8ab1d1-b10c-54c9-b5da-f9fa0821cec0
Slug: capability-selection-always-outside-ceiling
Domain: CFG · Subsystem: capability_selection

What happened

  • A Skill or tool is set to Always, but this request's settings don't allow it, for example because it is set to Never somewhere else. SMTO stopped rather than quietly widening what the agent may use.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Select Capabilities in the message box controls and check the Skill marked Always under each Apply to level: This prompt, This conversation and Global. An Always rule saved at one level can clash with a Never or narrower choice saved at another level.
  2. Either set that Skill to Auto to drop its Always rule, or, if you want it, make sure it isn't set to Never at any level. Then select Apply. Always only works for Skills the request is already allowed to use; it never grants extra permission.
  3. If you're sending in Ask mode, switch to Agent mode or remove Always rules for tools that make changes. Ask mode doesn't run tools that act on your computers, so Always rules for those tools can't apply.

What success looks like

  • Your message starts a task without this error.

If it still fails

  • If the request comes from a saved workflow or schedule, it may limit which tools it can use; select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't set more Skills to Always to get around this; Always never grants extra permission.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • An always_skill_ids or always_tool_ids entry in the capability selection configuration lies outside the request's compiled capability ceiling (effective policy, upstream workflow restrictions or Ask-mode tool limits), so acceptance was refused.

What this means

  • An Always Skill/tool ID falls outside the accepted compiled capability ceiling. The owning policy, configuration or publication transaction validates this state. Diagnostics do not grant authority, replace accepted snapshots, execute capabilities or publish a site; preserve the exact current decision and evidence.

Why this can happen

  • An Always Skill/tool ID falls outside the accepted compiled capability ceiling.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the Always rule with the effective ceiling and upstream restrictions; an Always flag never grants permission.

How to fix it

  • Compare the effective selection configuration's Always IDs with the compiled ceiling (skill_ids and tool_ids) for the request's prompt, conversation and global scopes, plus any upstream allowed-capability restriction. Remove the Always rule or deliberately enable the Skill or tool in the capability policy for new work; Always never widens the ceiling.
  • Remove the conflicting Always rule or deliberately change eligible capability policy through its supported owner for appropriate new work.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • Always rules fit the intended accepted authority without silently broadening it.

What not to do

  • Do not overwrite the original state with an incompatible version; use the supported upgrade path.

Technical notes

  • The owning policy, configuration or publication transaction validates this state. Diagnostics do not grant authority, replace accepted snapshots, execute capabilities or publish a site; preserve the exact current decision and evidence.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
